title: Drawing lines, circles and filling regions
subtitle: A screen has only whole pixels. These are the classic ways to choose which ones to light.

dda.title: The DDA line algorithm
dda.body: The DDA (digital differential analyser) steps along the longer axis one pixel at a time and adds the slope to the other coordinate, rounding each point: steps = max(|Δx|, |Δy|), x increment = Δx/steps, y increment = Δy/steps. It uses floating point and rounding in the loop. From (0,0) to (4,2) it lights 0,0 1,1 2,1 3,2 4,2.

bres.title: Bresenham’s line algorithm
bres.body: Bresenham keeps an integer decision (error) term saying whether the ideal line is closer to the pixel straight ahead or the one diagonally above. No multiplication or rounding: only additions and sign tests, hence its use in hardware. From (0,0) to (5,2): 0,0 1,0 2,1 3,1 4,2 5,2.

circle.title: The mid-point circle algorithm
circle.body: A circle is symmetric about both axes and the diagonals, so compute one octant (x from 0 to y) and reflect each point 8 ways. The mid-point method tests whether the midpoint between the two candidate pixels is inside the circle using a decision parameter p: start p₀ = 1 − r; if p < 0 keep y and p += 2x + 1, else y−− and p += 2(x − y) + 1. For r = 5 the first octant is 0,5 1,5 2,5 3,4.

fill.title: Filling: scan-line, boundary and flood fill
fill.body: Scan-line fill intersects each row with the polygon edges and fills between pairs of crossings (odd–even rule). Boundary fill starts inside and spreads until it meets a boundary colour; flood fill spreads through all pixels of the old colour. Both can use 4-connected neighbours (up, down, left, right) or 8-connected (plus diagonals); 8-connected fill can leak through a diagonal gap in a boundary drawn with 4-connected lines. The default pentagon fills 61 pixels.

attr.title: Aliasing and antialiasing
attr.body: Because pixels are discrete, slanted lines look stepped (aliasing). Antialiasing reduces it: supersample (compute at higher resolution and average), or shade edge pixels in proportion to how much of the pixel the line covers. The cost is more computation.

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• DDA: float increments; Bresenham: integers; circle: one octant + symmetry.
  • Fill by scan line, boundary or flood (4 vs 8 connectivity).
